title: Hypothyroidism & levothyroxine
summary: Read the TSH and FT4 together, then dose levothyroxine for the patient in front of you.

expansion: Young or middle-aged, healthy: full dose ≈ 1.6 mcg/kg/day
Older or long-standing disease, no heart disease: 50 mcg daily
Older with heart disease: 25 mcg daily

root.content: Fatigue, cold intolerance, weight gain, constipation

cards.text: TSH every 4–6 weeks; adjust by 12.5–25 mcg
Treat if TSH ≥ 10, or young/middle-aged with symptoms

cards.trapReason: The ATA recommends against routine levothyroxine + liothyronine combination therapy; benefits haven't been reproducible.
With a 7-day half-life, steady state takes 4–6 weeks. Checking sooner gives no clinical advantage.
In myxedema coma gut peristalsis stops, so every drug must be given parenterally.

s-myx.explanation: Mortality is 60%–70%. Give IV levothyroxine 300–500 mcg bolus (IV T3 has also been advocated) and IV hydrocortisone 100 mg every 8 h until adrenal suppression is ruled out. Treat the precipitant.

s-primary.explanation: TSH above and FT4 below the reference range is primary hypothyroidism. Hashimoto's (chronic autoimmune) thyroiditis is the most common cause.

s-drug.explanation: Levothyroxine is the drug of choice: stable, inexpensive, uniform potency, and a 7-day half-life allows once-daily dosing.

s-timing.explanation: Food impairs absorption, as do iron, calcium, PPIs, H2 blockers, bile acid sequestrants and others. Take it before breakfast on an empty stomach.

s-monitor.explanation: TSH is the most sensitive monitoring test. Check every 4–6 weeks and titrate by 12.5–25 mcg until TSH is normal, then yearly.

s-full.explanation: Start the full estimated dose (1.6–1.7 mcg/kg/day, better by ideal body weight) in young and middle-aged patients without significant comorbidities, and in iatrogenic hypothyroidism.

s-50.explanation: With long-standing disease or older age without known cardiac disease, start levothyroxine 50 mcg daily.

s-25.explanation: Older patients with known cardiac disease start at 25 mcg daily to avoid cardiac effects of over-replacement.

s-subclinical.explanation: High TSH with normal FT4 is subclinical. Most patients can be observed; it progresses to overt disease in 2%–5% per year.

s-subclin-treat.explanation: Treatment may be indicated when TSH is 10 mIU/L or higher, or in young and middle-aged patients with symptoms of mild hypothyroidism.

s-central.explanation: Low FT4 with a low or low-normal TSH is central (secondary or tertiary) hypothyroidism: the pituitary or hypothalamus isn't driving the gland.

s-central-monitor.explanation: TSH can't be used in central hypothyroidism. Dose to symptoms and FT4 in the upper part of normal (middle of normal in older or comorbid patients).
